title: Aliens
build: US Activision disk, 'Aliens [Activision].d64', a cracked copy: a Remember cracktro and trainer (22 KB BASIC file at $0801) in front of ten packed game files A0-A9

Starts the level: stops the music, turns off CIA 1's interrupts (so no tune plays), blanks the bitmap, points the raster call at $81AB and sets the VIC-II from the list after the call.
Clears the workspace, screen, colour and bitmap, selects VIC-II bank 1 and unpacks the picture (screen at $5C00, bitmap at $6000) from $E000, then sets up the lanes (lanes_init).
The JSR's operand; named by a stale reference.
The JSR's high byte.
unpack_inline's arguments: the packed data at $E000 ($E000), 4577 bytes long.
The packed picture's length.
Sets up the marine, the lanes and the sprites.

Once a frame, unless paused or over ($067B): moves the aliens, animates them, moves the marine and his flame, finds his lane, burns or pushes back the aliens there, counts the marines, the alien going for a marine, the fuse, the lane timers, the speeds, the score digits, new aliens, the alien dropping from the ceiling and the heartbeat.
One byte between the loop's JMP and heartbeat that nothing runs.
Every five ticks of $020B, $0661 goes up by one (to 22 at most), and the heartbeat sound beats faster: its gap is $36 less twice $0661.
The raster call at the top: the alien dropping from the ceiling (sprites 6 and 7), the flame (sprite 2) and the marine (sprite 3), then the lanes' raster calls from line $30.
Inside raster_top: the trainer pokes $8139 when it loads level 6, whose own code lies here then.
Inside raster_top: the trainer pokes $813A when it loads level 6, whose own code lies here then.
Inside raster_top: the trainer pokes $813B when it loads level 6, whose own code lies here then.
Inside raster_top: the trainer pokes $8178 when it loads level 4, whose own code lies here then.
For each lane, top to bottom: the upper halves of its two aliens (sprites 0 and 1), at their x and frames.
Six lines on: the lower halves (sprites 4 and 5), six pixels left of the upper halves except while the alien burns. Then the next lane, $0E lines further down, or the bottom row after the last.
After the last lane the raster call goes to line $AC (raster_bottom).
At line $B3: the marines still alive as a row of figures (sprites 0-6) and the alien going for them (sprite 7), then the fuse's spark.
At line $D0: the fuse's spark (sprite 0) at its place along the fuse, flickering white and red.
The next call at line $F8 (raster_frame).
At line $F8: level_frame, then the first raster call of the next frame.
Named by the trainer of level 1, which lies here when it is loaded.
Inside raster_frame: the trainer pokes $839D when it loads level 1, whose own code lies here then.
Inside raster_frame: the trainer pokes $839E when it loads level 1, whose own code lies here then.
The spark's y for each of the fuse's 40 steps.
The spark's x for each of the fuse's 40 steps.

The fuse: the spark moves to step $0675, and the fuse's next byte is drawn away in the bitmap (the address from fuse_addr, the byte from fuse_bytes, written into the STA at $8419). Every three ticks of $020B it burns one step on; at step 39 the level is won.
The fuse's bitmap address, written by fuse_tick.
Its high byte.
The level is won: the engine's stage_complete.
Places the row of marines left: sprite n at x from marines_x while n is less than the marines alive ($0680), otherwise at 0, out of sight.
The row's x for each marine.
When aliens have got past the marine ($066D) and none is on its way, the alien at the bottom sets off for the marines ($066E bit 7).

The alien walks left along the bottom ($066C) until it reaches the last marine in the row (grab_x by the marines alive). It takes him (grab_marine) and walks back to $C0; then one alien fewer has got past. With one marine left, it takes him and the level is lost: $0203 = 0 and stage_complete.
Where the alien reaches the last marine, by the number alive.
Takes a marine: clears the lowest set bit of the marines byte $0204.
The eight bits of the marines byte.

Each empty lane, when its timer has run, gets new aliens: one, then the other, then both (spawn_mask), coming in from the left. After the third wave the lane's aliens drop from the ceiling instead (drop_start).
Which aliens a lane's waves bring: a, b, then both.
An alien drops from the ceiling into the lane: sfx_alarm, a pause of 32 frames before the next, a random x, and the y where it lands ($85B8).
start_effect's argument: $3582 (sfx_alarm).
Sets the drop going.
The y where a dropping alien lands, by lane.
The dropping alien falls ($04A7 a frame); when it lands it becomes the lane's alien a, the lane counts one more ($0666) and its aliens get faster ($0613, by two after nine).
The burning aliens: each counts down from 7 through the burning frames ($8A0B, $8A0F); at the end it is gone, and an empty lane waits 7 ticks before its next wave.
The flame (sprite 2): a random colour from flame_colours; with fire held it shoots out from the marine and travels left ($04A5 a frame) up to 48 pixels, otherwise it is the idle frame by the gun.
The marine's lane: the one whose y is within $1A of his.
Each lane's y.

In the marine's lane: while the flame is out, an alien within 36 pixels of it starts burning (7); with the flame off, an alien that touches the marine is pushed back the way it came for 20 ticks less $0647, which grows by two with each push (to 12 at most), so each push is shorter.
The flame against the lane's two aliens.
Inside lane_hit: the trainer pokes $8798 when it loads level 5, whose own code lies here then.
Up and down on the joystick, unless fire is held: the marine's y $065C ($38-$A6, $04A4 a frame), his walking frame by y, and his x, which follows y ($78 plus a quarter of y) along the room's slant.
Moves each lane's aliens right by its speed ($049F), or back left while pushed. An alien that reaches x $B3 has got past the marine ($066D goes up) and the lane waits 32 ticks for its next wave.
Counts an alien a that got past; named by the trainer, whose level 3 cheat writes LDA here so none counts.
Counts an alien b that got past; also turned into an LDA by the trainer's cheat.
Aliens not in the lane are moved to x 0.
The aliens' upper frames, stepped every eight frames.
Inside aliens_frames: the trainer pokes $88A9 when it loads level 6, whose own code lies here then.
Inside aliens_frames: the trainer pokes $88AC when it loads level 6, whose own code lies here then.
The aliens' lower frames, stepped by their speed.
Inside aliens_legs: the trainer pokes $88B5 when it loads level 6, whose own code lies here then.
Each lane's speed $0495: $10 while pushed back, otherwise twice its count of landings ($0613), three times on its first wave.
A lane whose timer ($063C) has come round to the clock $0209 is free again.
The number of marines alive, the bits set in $0204, into $0680.
